answer.reasoning: None of the fitted candidates is acceptable: C8 and C9 have severe lack of fit, and C40 is also well beyond its 95% limit (484.0 vs 147.7), so it is not marginal. C40’s KS–Ki correlation is a caveat, not the reason for rejection; its parameters’ t-values are all above 1. The residual pattern motivates testing a different substrate-inhibition shape and biomass-dependent alternatives, since the experiments span different biomass levels and C40’s substrate residuals change direction across experiments.

candidates.reason: Test Haldane-type substrate inhibition as an alternative shape to the Andrews law, particularly to address the high-substrate E3 under-prediction.
Test a substrate-saturating law with positive biomass dependence, a distinct mechanism that can use the differing biomass levels across experiments.
Test biomass-dependent self-inhibition as a distinct mechanism; the experiments’ different starting biomass levels may help determine whether it explains the residual patterns.
